topic: Writing best practices for CLAUDE.md (DO/DON'T, length, style, anti-patterns, templates)

claims.quote: target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence
claims.paraphrase: Anthropic's explicit size target is under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md; beyond that, context cost rises and rule adherence drops.

claims.quote: A focused 30-line file outperforms a comprehensive 200-line file every time
claims.paraphrase: Community (dev.to docat0209) claims a 30-line rule outperforms 200-line files; shorter drives better compliance.

claims.quote: Under 60 lines in their root
claims.paraphrase: HumanLayer runs their own production CLAUDE.md under 60 lines at root, relying on progressive disclosure for the rest.

claims.quote: Metabase (~54 lines, Clojure): skills sections, tool preferences, backend test commands with imperative voice
claims.paraphrase: Metabase public CLAUDE.md stays around 54 lines with imperative commands and tool prefs - real-world lean benchmark.

claims.quote: LangGraphJS (33 lines, TypeScript): three sections - Build/Test, Code Style, Architecture
claims.paraphrase: LangGraphJS public CLAUDE.md is just 33 lines, 3-section structure - minimalist benchmark.

claims.quote: Start with Guardrails, Not a Manual. Your CLAUDE.md should start small, documenting based on what Claude is getting wrong
claims.paraphrase: Shrivu Shankar: build CLAUDE.md reactively from Claude's actual mistakes, not preemptively from everything imaginable.

claims.quote: facts Claude should hold in every session
claims.paraphrase: Mid-level abstractions = facts Claude must hold every session; not code-visible details, not platitudes.

claims.quote: WHAT / WHY / HOW
claims.paraphrase: HumanLayer structure for CLAUDE.md: WHAT (stack/architecture), WHY (purpose/non-obvious context), HOW (workflows/commands).

claims.quote: Use 2-space indentation instead of Format code properly
claims.paraphrase: Specific + verifiable beats vague: concrete rules ('2-space indent', 'run npm test before commit') outperform generic advice.

claims.quote: Language models struggle with negation. When you write 'Do NOT use semicolons,' the concept itself gets activated either way
claims.paraphrase: Positive over negative: negation still activates the prohibited concept; 'use named exports' beats 'no default exports'.

claims.quote: restrictions alone confuse agents trying to accomplish tasks
claims.paraphrase: Shrivu: prohibitions without alternatives confuse agents; always pair restriction with the preferred path.

claims.quote: Unlike CLAUDE.md instructions which are advisory, hooks are deterministic and guarantee the action happens
claims.paraphrase: CLAUDE.md is advisory (delivered as user message); hooks are deterministic enforcement - use hooks for hard rules.

claims.quote: If you have told Claude not to do something 3 times and it keeps doing it, move that rule from CLAUDE.md to a hook
claims.paraphrase: Three-strikes rule: if a CLAUDE.md prohibition fails 3+ times, migrate it to a hook or lint tool - don't just add CAPS.

claims.quote: CLAUDE.md content is delivered as a user message after the system prompt, not as part of the system prompt itself
claims.paraphrase: CLAUDE.md loads as user message after system prompt; no strict-compliance guarantee, which is why hooks trump it for enforcement.

claims.quote: A 500-token CLAUDE.md costs you 500 tokens on every single inference, and a 12,000-token skill file costs 12,000 tokens every time
claims.paraphrase: alexop.dev token math: CLAUDE.md is always-on cost per inference; a 2000-line bloat drains ~500+ tokens from every single turn.

claims.quote: information placed in the middle of long contexts is recalled less reliably than information at the beginning or end
claims.paraphrase: Lost-in-the-middle: rules buried mid-file in a 2000-line CLAUDE.md are ignored; primacy + recency bias favor top/bottom.
claims.source_ref: C11 (MindStudio on context rot); also referenced in C17

claims.quote: Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!
claims.paraphrase: Anthropic's own warning: bloated files trigger rule-dropping - the paradox where MORE rules yields LESS compliance.

claims.quote: Never send an LLM to do a linter's job. LLMs are comparably expensive and incredibly slow compared to traditional linters and formatters
claims.paraphrase: HumanLayer: don't put linter-enforceable rules (quotes, trailing commas, indent) in CLAUDE.md - run Biome/Prettier/ESLint instead.

claims.quote: exemplary CLAUDE.md files like pre-commit-hooks achieve quality through being 'thorough but not verbose' and avoid 'primarily consist[ing] in shouting at Claude in all-caps'
claims.paraphrase: awesome-claude-code meta-observation: quality = thorough-not-verbose; all-caps shouting (A5 anti-pattern) degrades emphasis signal.

claims.quote: if two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily
claims.paraphrase: Contradictions between root and nested CLAUDE.md cause arbitrary rule selection - hardest non-compliance to debug.

claims.quote: Don't Auto-Generate: Avoid /init or automated generation. Since this file 'affects every single phase of your workflow,' manual curation ensures quality
claims.paraphrase: HumanLayer: /init output is a draft, not a finished product; auto-generated 400-line boilerplate must be pruned manually.

claims.quote: Information that changes frequently
claims.paraphrase: Ephemera rule: task state, current sprint notes, TODO lists belong in plans/ folder (or GitHub issues), NOT in CLAUDE.md - which stays timeless.

claims.quote: use markdown headers and bullets to group related instructions. Claude scans structure the same way readers do
claims.paraphrase: Density vs readability: bullet-heavy structure beats dense prose; 80% bullets / 20% prose captions is the working ratio.

claims.quote: You can tune instructions by adding emphasis (e.g., 'IMPORTANT' or 'YOU MUST') to improve adherence
claims.paraphrase: Emphasis markers (IMPORTANT, YOU MUST) tune adherence when used sparingly - 2-3 times max; inflated usage nullifies the signal.

claims.quote: For complex X usage or if you encounter a FooBarError, see path/to/docs.md
claims.paraphrase: Shrivu 'pitch-don't-embed' (constitution model): instead of @imports for 500 lines of docs, write pointer sentences so Claude reads on demand.

claims.quote: Treat CLAUDE.md like code: review it when things go wrong, prune it regularly, and test changes by observing whether Claude's behavior actually shifts
claims.paraphrase: Anthropic: CLAUDE.md is code - version it, prune it, validate behavior shifts after edits (empirical testing, not one-shot write).

claims.quote: ./CLAUDE.md - team-shared (in git). ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md - personal preferences for all your projects. ./CLAUDE.local.md - personal + project-specific (in .gitignore)
claims.paraphrase: Three-tier separation: team project file, global user file, local gitignored file - prevents personal prefs colliding with teammates.

claims.quote: 5 complete starter templates: TypeScript/React (Next.js 15 + Prisma), Python ML (uv + polars + PyTorch), Rust CLI (cargo + clap), Monorepo (Turborepo + pnpm), Library/SDK (npm publish)
claims.paraphrase: Five drop-in starter templates 30-80 lines, stack-specific non-guessable commands + positive rules + 'Read when' reference docs.
claims.source_ref: R4 sections 11.1-11.5 (synthesizing C1, C2, C3, C6, C8, C10, C20-C27)

gaps_flagged: Exact tokenization cutoff where adherence drops (Anthropic says 200 lines, HumanLayer 60, dev.to 30 - no shared benchmark)
CLAUDE.local.md vs ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md boundary for personal prefs is fuzzy
Nested CLAUDE.md conflict resolution (deepest wins? ordering?) not documented by Anthropic
Managed-policy CLAUDE.md real-world enterprise examples absent from public research
@import performance ceiling at depth 2 vs 5 not benchmarked publicly
Empirical data on 3 bolded rules vs 30 bolded rules effectiveness missing
Interaction between CLAUDE.md and auto-memory (MEMORY.md) - boundary softer in practice than principle
<important if=...> tag effectiveness - community invention or hidden feature?
Threshold for 'multi-step procedure' when graduating CLAUDE.md rule to skill
